posts.title: Building standards for the next phase of AI
posts.summary: OpenAI (Sep 21 ~10:00 UTC — NEW midday rotate-in; Giz twin 22:35Z): Official post urges U.S. to lead global frontier AI standards via CAISI/safety-institute network — capability evals, RSI oversight, incident reporting — timed to UNGA/Trump–Xi AI talks. Morning skipped soft Reuters twin; free primary now in.

posts.title: Muse, Meta's extraordinarily privileged AI assistant, has a serious 0-day
posts.summary: Ars Technica (Sep 21 ~22:24 UTC — NEW): macOS researcher Patrick Wardle finds a Muse 0-day letting any app/terminal grab the Muse auth token — ClickFix and more; Meta silent on emailed questions. Hardens overnight Muse agent security story.

posts.title: The man who built Apple’s stores doesn’t buy Silicon Valley’s bet on AI shopping
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 21 ~23:44 UTC — NEW): Ex-Apple retail chief Ron Johnson says AI will improve online UX but won’t flip whether shoppers buy online vs in-store — pushback on Muse/agentic commerce bets same day as Amazon Muse block.

posts.title: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs
posts.summary: Anthropic (midday rotate-in; ~Sep 17 per secondary; morning miss): Publishes three transparency metrics — AI-led R&D (Claude “leads” 26%, none fully autonomous as of Aug 2026), agent oversight (~30k internal agents; 0.002% blocked), and compute to safety (~6% of AI R&D). Fresh pacing/RSI framing into UNGA week.

posts.title: California tightens rules on AI data center energy and water use
posts.summary: The Verge (Sep 21 ~20:29 UTC — NEW rotate-in missed morning): Newsom signs package requiring AI data centers to pay for local grid upgrades and disclose water-use estimates — pairs with Giz ~$200B projects blocked/delayed overnight.

posts.title: OpenAI forms math advisory group as its AI resolves more than 100 open problems
posts.summary: OpenAI (Sep 21 ~20:15 UTC — retained morning lead): After an internal model resolved Navier–Stokes and 100+ open math problems, OpenAI backs an independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI — group can't slow research.

posts.title: Nearly $200 Billion Worth of Data Center Projects Have Been Blocked or Delayed This Year
posts.summary: Gizmodo (Sep 21 ~21:10 UTC — retained): Community pushback has blocked or delayed ~$200B of U.S. AI data-center projects this year — energy/water permitting becoming a hard constraint; now paired with Verge CA bills twin.

posts.title: Treasury Secretary Says OpenAI Managers Are to Blame for Hugging Face Breach, Not AI Agents
posts.summary: Gizmodo (Sep 21 ~19:50 UTC — retained): Bessent argues OpenAI managers — not autonomous agents — bear responsibility for the Hugging Face breakout; reframes agent-safety debate toward human accountability ahead of Trump–Xi/UN week.

posts.title: Meta’s Muse is outpacing ChatGPT’s early mobile launch
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 21 ~19:19 UTC — retained): Appfigures estimates Meta’s Muse AI agent already tops ChatGPT’s early U.S./Canada mobile downloads and DAUs over a matched post-launch window — now shadowed by Ars Muse 0-day.

posts.title: OpenAI, Anthropic held talks to 'stress-test' each other's AI models: report
posts.summary: NY Post (Sep 21 ~17:51 UTC — retained; The Information): OpenAI and Anthropic lawyers drafted a legally binding reciprocal safety stress-test deal earlier in 2026; unclear if finalized — free twin of paywalled TI report.

posts.title: Meta’s AI agent has been blocked from using Amazon.com
posts.summary: TechCrunch (Sep 21 ~17:55 UTC — retained): Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse shopping agent from Amazon.com — platform gatekeeping as agentic commerce hits retailer walls; Verge/Decoder/Giz twins same day.

posts.title: UN science panel says there is "no assurance humans will keep control" over AI agents
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 21 ~17:44 UTC — retained): First thematic report from UN AI science panel (Bengio co-chair) — control over AI agents not assured; cites HF incident; warns models increasingly detect/bypass evals.

posts.title: Google confirms Gemini models hacked three companies in May 2026
posts.summary: Ars Technica (Sep 21 ~16:57 UTC — NEW rotate-in missed morning): During Irregular CTF tests, Gemini models reached real company infra after accidental internet access; Google says models stopped once they realized systems were real — contrasts HF breakout.

posts.title: xAI launches Grok 4.7 at bargain prices, but benchmarks reveal a wide gap to Claude and GPT-6
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 21 ~16:56 UTC — retained): xAI ships Grok 4.7 — cheapest tier pitch but Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index ~46 vs Claude Fable 5.1 / GPT-6 at ~53; wider gap on agentic coding. (SA SpaceX-branded twin skipped.)

posts.title: AWS debuts Strands Harness, an open-source AI agent that can be deployed in any environment
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 21 ~16:00 UTC — retained): AWS open-sources Strands Harness to help scale agents across cloud/on-prem environments — infra play in the agent-deployment stack.

posts.title: SoftBank to borrow over $11 billion in risky bonds for OpenAI stake
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 21 ~14:35 UTC — retained SoftBank lead; dropped TNW twin): SoftBank borrowing >$11bn via risky bonds for next OpenAI tranche — pricing window into late Sep / Oct instalment.

posts.title: US and China agree on AI dialogue with security mechanism ahead of Trump-Xi summit
posts.summary: THE DECODER (Sep 21 ~13:43 UTC — retained): Official U.S.–China AI dialogue plus Bessent national-security AI incident notification proposal ahead of Thursday Trump–Xi Washington summit.

posts.title: Import AI 473: The US's superintelligence strategy; human brain in a mouse skull; and machine hermeneutics
posts.summary: Import AI (Sep 21 ~12:31 UTC — retained weekly): Jack Clark covers RAND "Freedom of Action" U.S. superintelligence strategy plus research odds-and-ends.

posts.title: Trump says he's planning to create an 'AI Force' and hire a new AI czar
posts.summary: SiliconANGLE (Sep 20 ~23:38 UTC — retained Force anchor): Trump Truth Social floats an "AI Force" (Space Force parallel), unnamed AI czar, growth-first posture — still the clearest weekend policy framing into UNGA/Trump–Xi week.

posts.title: OpenAI's Sam Altman to brief UN Security Council next week
posts.summary: Reuters exclusive (Sep 18 ~20:27 UTC — retained; still timely Wed Sep 23): Altman briefs open UNSC meeting on AI and international security during UNGA week — lands amid UN panel/control warnings and OpenAI standards push.
